To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the NoSQL systems are a diverse set, (2) they are all based on some kind of distributed key value store, (3) they all provide some form of eventual consistency, and (4) they all provide different consistency guarantees, and different ways to control the consistency guarantees.
the new systems have different data models, different consistency models, and different storage and query models than relational databases.
the new systems are not a panacea for all problems, and that the choice of system depends on the application and its requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of scalable data stores that can support the needs of modern applications, and with the development of techniques for building applications on top of these stores.
understanding how to build large scale data systems that support the needs of modern applications.

the following questions: How can we build scalable data stores? What are their strengths and weaknesses? What is the right data store for a given application? What are the right applications for a given data store?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NoSQL is not a replacement for SQL.
the new systems are not "NoSQL", but "Not-just-SQL", and that they are a new generation of data management systems.
there is no single best data store.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NoSQL data stores are not suitable for OLTP applications that require strong ACID guarantees, while the SQL data stores are not appropriate for applications that need to scale to millions of concurrent users and/or need to store large volumes of data (e.g. more than 10TB) on a single machine.
there is no "one-size-fits-all" data store.
the new data stores are very different from traditional database systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NoSQL systems are a diverse set of data stores that are designed to scale simple application loads.
there are a number of different design choices that can be made in the context of a scalable data store, and that the right choice depends on a number of factors.
these systems can provide a good fit for some classes of applications, but not others.
